name: Production Database Credential Leak in Public S3 Bucket

input.title: Public S3 bucket credential leak with database passwords
input.description: AWS GuardDuty detected public access to s3://prod-database-backups which contained plaintext database credentials and API master keys.
input.impact: Production database passwords exposed to the public internet with active unauthorized access detected.
input.evidence: GuardDuty finding Stealth:IAMUser/AdminCredentialExposure; S3 access logs confirm GET requests from external IPs.
input.actions_taken: Revoked exposed IAM credentials, switched S3 bucket to private, and rotated production database passwords.

name: Total Outage of Authentication Service Core Flow

input.title: Total authentication service outage affecting all user logins
input.description: Auth service cluster is experiencing a complete outage with cascading 500 errors. All users are completely unable to login or refresh sessions.
input.impact: Total outage of primary auth flow; 100% of customer authentication requests failing globally.
input.evidence: Datadog alert: auth-service 5xx error rate at 100%; zero successful logins recorded over the last 15 minutes.
input.actions_taken: Restarted auth-service pods and rolled back latest deployment to restore service availability.

name: Partial Media Service Degradation with Available Workaround

input.title: Slow image uploads on media service with workaround available
input.description: Users uploading large PNG images experience intermittent 504 timeouts affecting approximately 5% of user uploads. JPEG uploads and smaller files function normally.
input.impact: Partial degradation affecting ~5% of users. Direct workaround available by converting images to JPEG format.
input.evidence: Prometheus media-worker metrics show p99 latency increased to 12s on PNG processing queues; error rate at 5.2%.
input.actions_taken: Routed large PNG uploads to auxiliary worker pool while engineering investigates image processing memory leak.

name: Cosmetic Footer Alignment Glitch on Mobile Safari

input.title: Styling misaligned in footer on mobile Safari
input.description: The footer copyright notice and navigation links overlap slightly by 8 pixels on iOS mobile Safari under iOS 17.
input.impact: Cosmetic issue only. No loss of functionality, no transactions affected, all links remain clickable.
input.evidence: Visual screenshot attached in ticket UI-2819 showing 8px margin overlap in viewport rendering.
input.actions_taken: Created frontend backlog ticket UI-2820 for upcoming sprint CSS adjustments.
